node.statement: Corrected threshold estimate (replacing the false strict estimate in node 1.2.1.2): because C_s={i:a_{is}>1-lambda}, membership i in C_s^c means a_{is}<=1-lambda and hence 1-a_{is}>=lambda. Since every mu_s(i)>=0, D_s=sum_i mu_s(i)(1-a_{is})>=sum_{i in C_s^c}mu_s(i)(1-a_{is})>=lambda*sum_{i in C_s^c}mu_s(i)=lambda*beta_s. Here lambda=sqrt(epsilon/2)>0, so beta_s<=D_s/lambda<=epsilon/(2*lambda)=lambda. Moreover epsilon<1/2 gives lambda=sqrt(epsilon/2)<1/2<1. Thus the weak inequality beta_s<=lambda asserted by the parent follows; no strict inequality beta_s<lambda is claimed or needed.
